title: SOV3 BFT Consensus Certificate Attestation Engine
filing_authority: MEOK Sovereign Substrate (SOV3) — IP-First AI Operating System
abstract: A Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) consensus engine for certificate attestation in multi-agent AI systems, operating without central certification authorities or trusted third parties. Unlike traditional certificate authorities (CAs) that rely on a central root of trust (X.509 PKI, Let's Encrypt, DigiCert) or blockchain-based certificates that require public global consensus (Ethereum EIP-3668, Solana Token Extensions), this invention implements a lightweight BFT council comprising 33 sovereign AI agents that collectively attest compliance certificates through a quorum-based voting mechanism (≥22/33 majority). Each certificate is issued as a signed HMAC-SHA256 payload by any council member, then circulated to the full council for quorum attestation. Attested certificates carry aggregated council signatures that any third party can verify against the council's published public-key set, requiring no network queries, blockchain lookups, or central registry. The engine operates in three phases: Phase 1 (Proposal) — any council member crafts a compliance attestation signed with their Ed25519 key; Phase 2 (Replication) — the proposal is broadcast to all council peers via a validated gossip protocol with tamper-evident delivery receipts; Phase 3 (Quorum) — each peer independently verifies the proposal against their local governance ruleset (a compact 21-rule SOV3 constitution), signs if approved, and returns the signature. Once ≥22 signatures (the BFT quorum) are collected, the certificate is considered 'attested' and carries the full quorum signature set. The BFT threshold is derived from the SOV3 charter's supermajority provision (§10.3) and ensures liveness even when up to 10 council members are compromised, offline, or adversarial. The engine includes an off-chain verifier (bft_cert_verifier.py) that can validate any attested certificate given only the council's public-key registry and the quorum signature payload, producing a human-readable verification report suitable for regulatory audit.

claims.claim: A Byzantine Fault Tolerant certificate attestation engine for multi-agent AI systems comprising: (a) a council of 33 sovereign AI agents each holding an Ed25519 keypair; (b) a three-phase protocol (Proposal, Replication, Quorum) for certificate issuance and collective attestation; (c) a quorum requirement of ≥22/33 council signatures for a certificate to be considered 'attested'; and (d) an off-chain verifier that validates attested certificates given only the council's public-key registry and the quorum signature payload.

The engine of claim 1, wherein Phase 1 (Proposal) comprises: a council member crafting a JSON compliance attestation payload; signing it with their Ed25519 private key; and embedding the signature as a 'proposal_signature' field before broadcasting to the council.

The engine of claim 1, wherein Phase 2 (Replication) comprises: a validated gossip protocol that delivers the proposal to all 33 council peers with tamper-evident delivery receipts; each receipt comprising HMAC-SHA256(receiver_peer_id || proposal_hash || received_timestamp); and a receipt chain that can be audited to confirm no message was dropped or modified in transit.

The engine of claim 1, wherein Phase 3 (Quorum) comprises: each peer independently verifying the proposal against a 21-rule SOV3 constitution; signing the proposal with their Ed25519 key if approved; returning the signature to the originating peer; and the originating peer aggregating signatures until the ≥22/33 quorum threshold is met, at which point the certificate carries the full quorum signature set for third-party verification.

The engine of claim 1, wherein the off-chain verifier produces a human-readable verification report containing: (a) the number of council signatures present vs required (≥22); (b) each signer's public key fingerprint and council position; (c) a hexadecimal digest integrity check of the original payload; and (d) a PASS/FAIL determination with supporting evidence for each of the 21 SOV3 constitution rules.

novelty_distinction: Traditional PKI (X.509, TLS, Web of Trust) relies on central CAs or hierarchical trust chains — a single compromised root CA can forge any certificate in the chain. This engine distributes trust across 33 sovereign agents with a BFT quorum, providing liveness even when 10 members are compromised.

Blockchain-based certificates (Etheremi Attestation Service, Solana Token Extensions, Ceramic) require global consensus, gas fees, and network queries for verification. This engine produces self-contained certificates with embedded quorum signatures — verifiable offline with zero network calls.

Existing BFT systems (PBFT, HotStuff, Tendermint) focus on state-machine replication and transaction ordering, not certificate attestation. This engine is purpose-built for compliance certification with a domain-specific 21-rule constitution for peer validation.

The three-phase protocol (Proposal → Replication → Quorum) with tamper-evident delivery receipts is novel in the certificate attestation domain, combining BFT consensus with auditable message delivery guarantees.

No existing system provides an off-chain verifier that can validate a BFT council-attested certificate against a constitutional rule set without network queries — this enables verification in air-gapped environments, regulatory filings, and court proceedings.
